free_tier.stated: Unlimited total: 'The total volume and number of your files are unlimited'. Free unregistered uploads are capped at 200 MB; registered free accounts go much higher (operator advertises up to 100 GB file transfer volume).
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: file size ceiling well above 200 MB
per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Free downloads: ~5 GB/day per user with a hard speed cap and IP queueing. Turbo: 40 GB/day and 600 GB/month. No per-GB price.

tooling: Turbobit Uploader desktop app, FTP upload, and third-party rclone/JDownloader support; no first-party public REST API documented.
chaining: Unlimited total per account is the headline; with email-only registration the chain is N accounts. The 40 GB/day cap is per *download* identity, so serving volume scales with IPs, not accounts.

limits.value: file size ceiling well above 200 MB

limits_note: Registered free: file size ceiling well above 200 MB (unregistered 200 MB). Retention: files expire after inactivity ('storage time expiration' is a listed deletion reason). Free download ~5 GB/day, 55-60 KB/s class throttling on the sister host. Turbo 40 GB/day, 600 GB/month.

identity_cost.detail: derived from the record's prose, not from an identity field, and no signup was executed: rottling on the sister host. Turbo 40 GB/day, 600 GB/month. anonymous-dump

reliability_note: Free-tier serving is throttled to dial-up speeds and gated behind a human-verification step and a queue, so it works as storage but not as a fetch origin. Dyna mic Download Splitting means the previous file's size sets your next wait.
